macro_objective: Students write a persuasive letter that states a claim, supports it with reasons and evidence, and answers an opposing view.

mls_units.title: Taking Arguments Apart
mls_units.macro_alignment: Gives students the claim, reason, evidence and opposing-view parts they will build their own letters from, by finding them in two real opinion pieces.

tasks.action: Write the four parts of an argument on the board: claim, reasons, evidence, answer to an opposing view. Show each part in one short opinion paragraph read aloud to the class.
In pairs, read opinion piece A and mark its claim, each reason, the evidence for each reason, and any answer to an opposing view. Partners take turns reading aloud and marking.
In the same pairs, mark the four parts in opinion piece B, which argues the other side of the same local issue.
Build a class chart on chart paper comparing the two pieces part by part. Ask pairs which piece supports its reasons better and why, and write their reasons on the chart.

mls_units.title: Writing and Revising a Persuasive Letter
mls_units.macro_alignment: Turns the four argument parts into each student's own finished persuasive letter, revised after feedback.

tasks.action: Recall from MLS-PERSUADE-01: use the class chart of the four argument parts. Each student chooses an issue in their school or neighbourhood and writes a one-line claim and three reasons in their notebook.
Give a full lesson of quiet writing time. Each student drafts a one-page letter that states the claim, supports each reason with evidence, and answers one opposing view.
In pairs, read each other's draft and check it against the four parts on the class chart. Each partner writes one note on what is missing or unclear, then partners swap roles.
Give a second full lesson for each student to revise the draft using the partner's note and write a final copy.
